source: GSMA + central bank reports + Mordor Intelligence + Statista + fintech media (Fintech News SG/ID/PH, Tech in Asia, Reuters)
methodology: Top provider share = market share of #1 wallet/rail in mobile payments. Where retail e-wallet share and instant-payment rail share are reported separately, the dominant rail (e.g. PromptPay, Bakong) is treated as backbone if it carries the bulk of P2P/merchant volume. Estimates for KH/LA/MM/BN are media-derived due to absence of granular regulator data.

VN.notes: MoMo ~56% (31M active), ZaloPay ~23%, VNPay ~15%. Top5 (incl ViettelPay, ShopeePay) ~65% per Mordor 2025. Platform-driven, telco-affiliated VNPT/Viettel marginal.

ID.notes: Highly fragmented: GoPay/OVO/DANA/ShopeePay each 15-25%. Top5 ~70% combined per Mordor 2025. QRIS (central bank standard) used by all wallets as interoperability layer but commercial rails remain platform-driven.

PH.notes: Extreme concentration. GCash ~85-89% (81M users 2024), Maya ~13-15%. GCash owned by Globe Telecom + Ant Group + Mynt - hybrid telco/platform but operationally platform-driven super-app.

TH.notes: PromptPay (BoT-mandated rail) handles ~41% of mobile payments and 74M tx/day, 90M+ registrations. In wallet segment alone TrueMoney leads (~53%) but PromptPay dominates overall P2P/merchant volume across all bank apps.

MY.notes: TNG eWallet 62% preference (20M+ users), MAE #2 ~12%, GrabPay/ShopeePay/Boost trail (~5-9% each). DuitNow QR (central bank) provides interoperability but does not concentrate volume.

SG.notes: PayNow is bank-consortium rail (MAS-supervised, ABS-operated) - 5M+ registrations, near-universal. Wallet segment: DBS PayLah! 26%, GrabPay 35.3%, ShopeePay smaller. Backbone = bank consortium rather than central bank or single platform.

KH.notes: Bakong (NBC-operated blockchain rail) processed 75.6M tx in H1 2024 (+180% YoY); KHQR standard. Wing Bank #2 (~17% e-com share), TrueMoney small (~2%). Strong central-bank backbone.

LA.notes: BCEL One (state-owned commercial bank) dominates urban QR. U-Money (Unitel/Viettel telco) #2, LDB and JDB smaller. Mobile money +20% YoY but absolute volumes low. Limited regulator data - figures are media-derived estimates.

MM.notes: KBZPay (KBZ Bank) 19M users 2024, 43% adult population, 2.1B tx in 2024 - now larger than Wave Money. Wave Money ~30% (telco-origin, formerly 80% pre-2021). Ooredoo Money small. Backbone shifted from telco (Wave) to bank (KBZ) post-coup.

BN.notes: BIBD holds 56% retail deposits / 65% loans; NEXGEN wallet = 90% of BIBD retail tx. Baiduri Bank #2. Very small market (~150K active NEXGEN users) but extreme bank concentration. Quickpay QR is BIBD-proprietary.

hypotheses.statement: Platform-backbone countries (VN, ID, PH, MY) show higher fragility to corporate failure: a single super-app outage (GCash, MoMo, GoPay, TNG) can freeze 50%+ of national retail payments.
hypotheses.evidence: PH (GCash 85%) and VN (MoMo 56%) have no public-rail fallback. ID is mitigated by QRIS interoperability despite platform dominance.

hypotheses.statement: Central-bank-backbone countries (TH PromptPay, KH Bakong) are structurally more resilient because the rail is non-profit, regulator-operated, and interoperable across all licensed wallets/banks.
hypotheses.evidence: PromptPay's 74M daily tx flow continues regardless of any commercial wallet's solvency. Bakong's blockchain settlement decouples from individual provider risk.

hypotheses.statement: Telco-backbone is effectively extinct in ASEAN-10 as of 2025-2026: Wave Money (MM) lost dominance to KBZ Bank post-2021 coup; ViettelPay (VN) remains marginal. Telco-led mobile money model has been displaced by either platform super-apps or central-bank rails.
hypotheses.evidence: No ASEAN-10 country has telco as #1 in 2025. Contrasts with East Africa (M-Pesa Kenya). Implication: M-Pesa template did not transfer to ASEAN.

hypotheses.statement: Concentration (top1 share) correlates inversely with GDP per capita above a threshold: smaller/poorer markets (BN, PH, MM, KH) show 60-85% top-1 share; larger/wealthier markets (ID, SG) show 25-35%.
hypotheses.evidence: ID's 270M population sustains 4+ competitive wallets; BN's 0.45M population sustains only 1 dominant bank. Network effects + market-size threshold for competitive entry.

hypotheses.statement: Hybrid backbone (bank consortium like SG PayNow, or central-bank-mandated interop like ID QRIS, TH PromptPay) is the most resilient configuration - reduces both single-platform failure risk AND single-regulator-policy risk.
hypotheses.evidence: SG and ID both maintain wallet competition (low HHI) while standardizing the rail. KH Bakong is centralized but lacks competing wallet ecosystem - single-point-of-policy risk.

data_quality_warnings.notes: LA and BN figures rely on bank annual reports and single-source media estimates; regulator-published share data unavailable. KH Bakong share inferred from transaction volume growth, not formal HHI.
